title: Tojo takes power
photoNote: Official portrait of Hideki Tojo, 1941. Public domain (Japanese photograph published before 1957). Check license on Commons.
body:
Seven weeks before Pearl Harbor, an army general took charge of Japan's government.

18 October 1941. General Hideki Tojo became prime minister. Two days earlier, Prince Konoe had resigned, politically isolated and convinced the emperor no longer trusted him.

Tojo did not give up his old job. He stayed on as Army Minister and took over the Home Ministry too. Colleagues called him "Razor" for his sharp, quick mind.

He took office with orders to re-examine Japan's options for dealing with the United States. On 7 December 1941, Japan attacked Pearl Harbor.

declassified.fact: While Tojo awaited his war crimes trial in Sugamo Prison, a young U.S. Navy dentist named Jack Mallory made him new dentures and secretly drilled "Remember Pearl Harbor" into them in Morse code. When the story reached an American radio station, Mallory had to wake Tojo one night and grind it off. Tojo apparently never knew.

sources.title: The American Dentist Who Drilled a Secret Message on Tojo's Dentures, Mental Floss
